explanation: Matches erdosproblems.com/1056: for every k ≥ 2 there are a prime p and k consecutive intervals [b_i, b_{i+1}) (b strictly increasing) whose products are all ≡ 1 mod p. The bounds are not restricted to below p, but this changes nothing: an interval containing a multiple of p has product 0, so all intervals sit inside one block between consecutive multiples of p, which reduces to residues 1..p-1. The formalization allows the trivial interval {1}. Since a k-interval solution starting with {1} yields a (k-1)-interval solution starting at 2, the 'for all k' statement is equivalent to the version with nontrivial intervals.
